summary: Returns the value as an absolute path, or throws.
description: A path that starts at a root: a leading `/`, or a scheme such as `https://` or `mailto:`. Everything else, the empty string included, is relative.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, typed as an absolute path.

throws.IllegalArgumentException: the value is not an absolute path.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireAbsolute("/var/log"); // => "/var/log"
requireAbsolute("https://example.com/a"); // => "https://example.com/a"
requireAbsolute("docs/readme.md"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireAbsolute("./a"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
